b2084127df.q: Why did major real estate syndicators like Tides Equities and S2 Capital lose hundreds of millions in LP equity during the 2022-2024 real estate downturn?
b2084127df.a: These syndicators became fashionable in using bridge debt on multifamily value-add deals while assuming prices would keep rising, without considering that rates could go up drastically and quickly. The incentive structure pushed them to do deals regardless of risk: acquisition fees and asset management fees comprised 50% or more of their total compensation, while the remaining carry depended on back-end performance. When the market shifted, their front-loaded fees protected them personally even as investor returns collapsed to 5-10% IRR instead of projected 18-20%.

4f1efc080c.q: What is the current valuation discount for U.S. multifamily public REITs in 2024-2025?
4f1efc080c.a: U.S. multifamily public REITs are trading at 70 cents on the dollar, meaning their stock price is 70 cents for every dollar of asset value they own. Some of these REITs are even buying back their own stocks at these depressed valuations.

b541e4f655.q: Why did Paul Shannon decide not to scale aggressively in 2022 and maintain fixed-rate debt instead of bridge debt like competitors?
b541e4f655.a: Shannon studied financial history and recognized that when Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell shifted commentary from transitory inflation to structural inflation, interest rates could rise drastically and quickly. He observed that acquisitions with floating-rate debt at compressed cap rates and high prices assumed continuous rent growth, which was unsustainable. By staying conservative with fixed-rate agency debt, he positioned his portfolio to avoid the massive losses his competitors faced while maintaining investor trust.

7f4f5096d9.q: What are the new return expectations and investment thesis for multifamily real estate in 2025 compared to the 2011-2019 period?
7f4f5096d9.a: Returns have shifted from projected 20% IRRs to longer hold periods with lower returns, typically focused on diversification, tax benefits, and in-place cashflow rather than appreciation. Successful investments require conservative underwriting with decent basis, conservative debt, in-place cashflow, conservative rent growth assumptions, and strong operating teams that can control expenses, rather than the previous strategy of buying, assuming rent growth, and relying on debt being cheap.
